published_results.metric: token savings % of stacked RTK→Caveman compression on eligible tool/context payloads. The number is computed from upstream third-party README figures, not measured: RTK https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk (60-90%, sample ~118,000→~23,900 tokens = 79.7%) and Caveman https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman (~46% input, 65% avg / ~75% headline / 22-87% output)
published_results.baseline: uncompressed payload; formula combined = 1 - (1 - RTK) * (1 - Caveman_input)

summary: OmniRoute's headline '15–95% tokens (~89% avg)' is arithmetic on third-party README figures: the docs combine RTK's 60-90% and Caveman's ~46% input savings as 1 − (1 − RTK) × (1 − Caveman_input), giving 78.4–94.6% and an 89.2% average. The per-mode figures (Lite ~15%, Standard ~30%, Aggressive ~50%, Ultra ~75%) and the 69 → 19 token (72%) example are stated without data. The harness-backed numbers are narrower: a committed CI floor of compressed tokens per task over a 5-case corpus (`npm run check:compression-budget`), which records no uncompressed counts and lists the same values (129 / 127 / 160) for lite, aggressive, rtk, session-dedup and headroom; a unit test that runs the single input behind the quoted 95.93% (300 identical error lines) and asserts savings above 90%; and a routing-event microbenchmark (`npm run bench:routing-events`, ~0.12 µs of event-dispatch overhead per request). Other harnesses (bench:compression, eval:compression, perf:lts-baseline) have no committed outputs.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
